chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban and Yahya, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who gives a man money and says to him, 'Go to such and such land and do not exceed it; buy from it.' He (the Imam) said: 'If he exceeds it and the money is lost, he is liable (guarantor); if he buys something and it is placed (in storage/possession), it is upon him; and if he profits, it is between them (shared).'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial liabilities and profit-sharing rules when an agent exceeds their authorized trading area in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the foundational principles of *al-mudarabah* (profit-sharing partnership) by defining the agent's liability for loss if they exceed the designated geographical boundary. It clarifies that ownership transfers upon possession (*qabd*) and profits are shared, reflecting the early juristic consensus on risk allocation in commercial agency. This hadith is pivotal in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between fixed-fee agency (*mu'awadha*) and profit-sharing models, emphasizing the agent's role as a trustee (*amin*) unless negligence or deviation occurs.
